name: OpenLink Virtuoso
tagline: Hybrid SQL/RDF engine that runs many of the largest public SPARQL endpoints.
description: OpenLink Virtuoso is a long-lived hybrid server that combines a column-store relational engine with native RDF storage, SPARQL 1.1, SQL and SPASQL (SPARQL inside SQL), plus a web and Linked Data server. It powers well-known public endpoints such as DBpedia and UniProt, which shows it can serve billions of triples to anonymous traffic. The open-source edition (GPLv2, 7.2.x line, last release 7.2.17 in May 2026) is single-server; the commercial edition adds elastic clustering and replication. It is a pragmatic choice for big Linked Data publishing, though its tooling and documentation feel dated.

license.name: GPL-2.0 (Open Source Edition); commercial edition proprietary

pricing.notes: Open-source edition is free; commercial edition (clustering, replication) is licensed, and AMIs are sold on AWS Marketplace.

scale.notes: Single-server in the open-source edition; the commercial Elastic Cluster shards across nodes.

strengths: Proven at serving billions of triples on public endpoints such as DBpedia and UniProt
Column-store indexes with compression keep large RDF datasets compact
SQL and SPARQL in one engine, including SPARQL embedded inside SQL
Bundled web server, WebDAV and Linked Data publishing features
weaknesses: Open-source edition has no clustering; scale-out is commercial-only
Dated admin UI (Conductor) and scattered documentation
Query planner can behave unpredictably on complex SPARQL, needing manual tuning
Small vendor with slow open-source release cadence
useCases: Large RDF datasets in life sciences
Hybrid SQL plus RDF data integration
notIdealFor: Property-graph apps using Cypher or Gremlin
